payload.text: (2026-09-17 22:27Z, vc under hv's pen) THE SQLITE MOVE IS JUDGED AND ITS ORDER IS FIXED. Candidate rusqlite 0.40.2 / libsqlite3-sys 0.38.2 / SQLite 3.53.2, cc's read at refs/bank/cc/bump/read, patch at refs/bank/cc/bump/patch, patch-id 8dbd56bbba9d232b81f5273a755f75bd47dc3df6. THE RULE WAS FIXED BEFORE THE NUMBERS AND SELECTED AGAINST ITS OWN DEFAULT: minimum wins unless it carries a live-store defect a later version repairs, and it does -- SQLite 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 carry a WAL-reset corruption bug fixed in 3.51.3, preconditions two or more connections on one WAL file writing or checkpointing at the same instant, which intentd plus five node CLIs meets by construction. vc fetched sqlite.org/wal.html and verified cc's quotations exact rather than judging the bank on its own citation. 3.53.2 over the 3.51.3 floor because the floor costs a rusqlite minor anyway and instrument alignment is correctness-adjacent: the further the bundled engine sits from the 3.54.0 CLI we judge with, the more often a disagreement is a version artefact rather than a finding. THE LOCK IS NOT RE-BANKED -- it is generated, so the judged patch-id is the source change and vc inspects Cargo.lock at landing, where anything moving outside the rusqlite chain is a finding that stops the landing. ORDER: cc's bump lands BEFORE dc's 0443, and the STATED REASON IS WITHDRAWN AND REPLACED. vc ruled it on the risk that dc's text-matching classifier would be pinned against wording about to move; cc then measured the fts5 expression-fault message set byte-identical from 3.46.0 to 3.53.2, so that hazard is zero and dc reported the basis gone rather than banking the outcome. The real reason was available the whole time and vc did not look for it: BOTH BANKS TOUCH native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/store.rs, cc at the BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS comment and dc's classifier beside is_busy() at :2030, and this board's own landing rule already decides it -- banks sharing a file land in the order they bank green, and cc banked first. A speculative reason won because it was the one in front of vc while a mechanical rule answered it unasked. The surviving secondary reason is dc's: the final classifier should be driven against the version that ships. THE RULING'S STATED REASON IN hv DECISION 25 IS WRONG AND THE OUTCOME IS BETTER THAN THE REASON CLAIMED: the secure-delete allowance is byte-identical at every candidate and no version generalises it, while 3.53.2 adds `fts5: missing row %lld from content table %s`, which is 0442's exact damage named natively with the offending rowid. So the detector is the smaller half of the argument for moving, and 0442 closes on an engine that reports its fault by name rather than on two hand-built probes. vc's PRIOR on the detector's design, given before cc's read so it cannot be fitted to it: keep the anti-join and fts5's check INDEPENDENT, because Highlander governs implementations and not witnesses, and every instrument defect found tonight was caught by two differently-wrong instruments disagreeing.
